decisions.reason: ERC-721C royalty enforcement does not change which book access, referral identity, badges, or prize-ticket states follow an NFT after an allowed transfer.
Selecting ERC-721C instead of plain ERC-721 does not change the confirmed Base deployment network.
The source changes the NFT contract standard and secondary-market enforcement mechanism but does not change any currently required metadata field or visibility rule.
The existing FAQ requirement discloses the royalty but does not require naming the NFT standard or Creator Controls; the source does not request a FAQ copy change.
The secondary-market NFT standard and royalty controls do not alter the deferred Transak provider, fiat methods, wallet provisioning, or primary-mint destination.
Using ERC-721C does not change the asset being an NFT ebook or its unlimited edition supply.
ERC-721C retains ERC-721 ownership semantics, so Lit Protocol can continue checking Base NFT ownership without changing the access eligibility, provider, or automatic ownership-check requirement.
The royalty-enforcement standard does not change the Small Block winner count, prize amount, sales trigger, or pool-allocation rules.
Choosing ERC-721C for secondary royalty enforcement does not change automatic prize payout behavior.
The NFT standard and marketplace whitelist do not affect the curated badge set, icons, or badge presentation choices.
The ERC-721C decision does not change referral milestone thresholds or the requirement to attach earned badges on-chain to the NFT.
Secondary-market royalty enforcement is independent of the Chainlink VRF provider, on-chain selection, fairness, verification surface, and applicable Small Block draw.
